notes: First successful end-to-end generation of gpt-oss-120b on an 8 GB laptop. Output: 'The capital of France is Paris.'

This is exactly the regime where a custom expert loader should win: read whole 13 MB experts with large O_DIRECT/overlapped reads instead of faulting 3,300 x 4 KB pages each. That alone would move I/O from ~300 MB/s (fault-bound) toward 510 MB/s (device-bound), and stop stalling 3 cores.

The 8 GB laptop is not a fair test of the cache THESIS (routing-aware vs LRU) because capacity is below one token's working set -- there is nothing to cache. It IS a fair test of the LOADER thesis (bulk expert reads vs 4 KB mmap faults).

diagnosis: PAGE-FAULT-BOUND, not compute-bound and not device-bound. The page cache (~2.5 GB after the process's own working set) is smaller than one token's 3.27 GB demand, so every token evicts most of the previous token's experts. mmap then re-faults them in 4 KB units at ~75k faults/s, which saturates the fault handler at ~300 MB/s -- 59% of the SSD's 510 MB/s -- while 3 of 4 cores sit idle. 3.27 GB / 0.30 GB/s = 10.9 s/token predicted vs 12.9-19.7 measured. capacity.py assumed I/O at device bandwidth in large blocks; that assumption is what was wrong.
